profile.entities: Sagar Cements Ltd (Parent); Andhra Cements Ltd (Subsidiary)
profile.themes: Andhra Cements Turnaround; Vizag Land Monetisation; Capacity Expansion (Jeerabad/Dachepalli); Debt Reduction

bull_bear.body: Priority: Debt reduction. Vizag land monetisation expected to yield ~₹350cr net over next 18 months (5-6 tranches). Target D/E ratio to improve to ~0.5x in 18-24 months. No major M&A or greenfield CapEx planned until FY29.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Delay in Vizag land policy approval; Volatility in pet coke/domestic coal prices; Competitive pressure from UltraTech (Line-4) and Ramco (Kolimigundla Line-2) capacity additions in AP; Sustained low utilization at Jajpur and Dachepalli plants.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; Focused on operational efficiency and balance sheet repair; Transparent about Andhra Cements' cost gaps but confident in imminent breakeven.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Depreciation spike is due to capitalization of completed CapEx (preheater/WHRS) rather than accounting policy change; Fuel cost variance in presentations due to 'as-fired' basis shift highlighting Singareni coal usage at Mattampally vs. imported coal elsewhere.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: State Mix: Telangana (28%), Andhra Pradesh (28%), Odisha (10%), Maharashtra (9%), MP (8%), Karnataka (7%), TN (6%), Gujarat (3%). Plant Utilization: Jeerabad (95%), Gudipadu (82%), Mattampally (57%), Bayyavaram (66%), Jajpur (40%), Dachepalli (39%).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| High cost structure at Andhra Cements nearing breakeven; Volume growth in South India | Sagar Cements Limited | beneficiary | Med | Turnaround play dependent on successful Vizag land monetisation to clean up balance sheet and full realization of Q4 price hikes. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: Q3 Power & Fuel: ₹1,408/tonne (down from ₹1,456); Freight: ₹830/tonne. Q4 Cost Savings expected: WHRS at Gudipadu (₹100-125/tonne saving), Jeerabad grinding mill (₹150-200/tonne fixed cost leverage), Andhra electrical efficiency (₹25-50/tonne). Fuel price outlook: Flat for FY26, +2-3% for FY27.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Volume: 6.0 Mn tonnes for FY26 (9% growth), 7.0 Mn tonnes for FY27; EBITDA/tonne: ₹500-525 for FY26, ₹500-550 for Q4FY26; Capex: ₹489cr (FY26), ₹291cr (FY27).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Not applicable for cement commodity sales; Demand outlook: High single-digit growth in AP/Telangana, flat in TN, 3-5% in Karnataka.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Jeerabad expansion (1.0 to 1.5 Mn tonnes) by Q1 FY27; Dachepalli capacity addition by Aug 2026; Long-term target of 12-15 Mn tonnes with major CapEx starting FY29.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Sagar Cements posted flattish EBITDA (₹38cr) despite 8% volume growth due to high costs at Andhra Cements, but guided for a sharp Q4 recovery to ₹500-550/tonne EBITDA driven by price hikes and Andhra's breakeven. The strategic pivot focuses on retiring debt via ₹350cr Vizag land monetisation over 18 months rather than immediate capex expansion.
